svg.title: Single cells of one leukemia grouped into clones, and the tree of the clones
svg.desc: Schematic after Gawad, Koh and Quake, PNAS 111:17947 (2014), Fig. 2, for one patient in place of the paper's six. Left: a heat map with one row for each of 46 single cells and one column for each of 20 mutations; a dark cell means the mutation was found in that cell. A color bar on the right groups the rows into three clones: clone 1 (24 cells), clone 2 (14 cells) and clone 3 (8 cells). Cells of one clone carry nearly the same mutations, with scattered light gaps inside the dark blocks where a mutation was missed in a cell. Two mutations are in all three clones, eight only in clone 1, six in clones 2 and 3 and four only in clone 2. Right: the tree of the clones, with time running downward. From the founding cell one branch leads to clone 1 and another to clone 3; clone 2 descends from clone 3. The area of each circle shows the number of cells in the clone. The pattern is illustrative, laid out like the paper's patient 1; it is not the paper's cell-by-cell data.
